workload_queue_combined·workload_queue_combined·cpu_dblade_background_service_time·cpu_dblade_background_service_time·iops_total·"direct,wafl_cp,background_delete,readahead_x_stripe"·"The average CPU Dblade background service time per operation. This is the CPU service time for background operations done for this workload in the Dblade. Direct represents service time directly tallied for the workload. Wafl_cp represents service time contributed by the WAFL_CP workload on behalf of this workload. The WAFL_CP workload performs disk write operations. Background_delete represents service time contributed by the BACKGROUND_DELETE workload on behalf of this workload. The BACKGROUND_DELETE workload performs block deletions on disks. Readahead_x_stripe represents service time contributed by the RA_STRIPE_X workload on behalf of this workload. The RA_STRIPE_X workload performs read-ahead operations to improve disk read performance. Units are microseconds."·"The average CPU Dblade background service time per operation. This is the CPU service time for background operations done for this workload in the Dblade. Direct represents service time directly tallied for the workload. Wafl_cp represents service time contributed by the WAFL_CP workload on behalf of this workload. The WAFL_CP workload performs disk write operations. Background_delete represents service time contributed by the BACKGROUND_DELETE workload on behalf of this workload. The BACKGROUND_DELETE workload performs block deletions on disks. Readahead_x_stripe represents service time contributed by the RA_STRIPE_X workload on behalf of this workload. The RA_STRIPE_X workload performs read-ahead operations to improve disk read performance. Units are microseconds."·average,no-zero-values·array·false·-·

workload_queue_combined·workload_queue_combined·delay_cop_num_wait·delay_cop_num_wait·-·-·"This captures the number of times, ops are suspended/ delayed as COP (Container OverProvisioning) subsystem makes the volume ready for accepting work, aggregated cluster-wide. This can be either introduced as the volume is transitioned from COP passive state to active state. Or, it can be introduced when a volume is explicit restrained to be dirtied in the next CP (Consistency Point), which might be already overloaded. workload_queue_combined·workload_queue_combined·iops·iops·-·"read,write,other"·"This is the rate of workload operations that completed during the measurement interval, as measured at the N-blade layer. This counter also serves as the base counter for total_latency, the one other counter in this object that shares its exact 3-element (read/write/other) shape. Every other averaged delay/service-time counter below (nblade- and dblade- origin, none of which have a per-op-type breakdown) uses the iops_total counter instead. There is no native dblade-side operation count, so this N-blade rate is reused as an approximation when averaging dblade-origin counters below."·"This is the rate of workload operations that completed during the measurement interval, as measured at the N-blade layer. This counter also serves as the base counter for total_latency, the one other counter in this object that shares its exact 3-element (read/write/other) shape. Every other averaged delay/service-time counter below (nblade- and dblade- origin, none of which have a per-op-type breakdown) uses the iops_total counter instead. There is no native dblade-side operation count, so this N-blade rate is reused as an approximation when averaging dblade-origin counters below."·rate,no-zero-values·array·false·-·
workload_queue_combined·workload_queue_combined·iops_total·iops_total·-·-·"This is a convenience counter: the scalar sum of iops[read] + iops[write] + iops[other]. It exists solely to serve as the base counter (denominator) for the scalar (and 4-element background-service-time) averaged counters below, none of which have a per-op-type breakdown of their own. iops itself is a 3-element array and cannot be used directly as a base counter for a scalar or differently-shaped average - only total_latency, which shares iops's exact 3-element shape, can divide against iops element-by-element. Typed CM_CNT_DELTA so clients can cook this counter themselves if they wish. A base counter's own declared type has no effect on the AVERAGE division, which always operates on raw sample deltas regardless of it."·"This is a convenience counter: the scalar sum of iops[read] + iops[write] + iops[other]. It exists solely to serve as the base counter (denominator) for the scalar (and 4-element background-service-time) averaged counters below, none of which have a per-op-type breakdown of their own. iops itself is a 3-element array and cannot be used directly as a base counter for a scalar or differently-shaped average - only total_latency, which shares iops's exact 3-element shape, can divide against iops element-by-element. Typed CM_CNT_DELTA so clients can cook this counter themselves if they wish. A base counter's own declared type has no effect on the AVERAGE division, which always operates on raw sample deltas regardless of it."·delta,no-zero-values·-·false·-·
